_about: Quest Forge client profile. Read by tools/lite-client/apply-profile.ps1 on Windows and by the Mac's Prism tooling. Keys that start with _ are comments. Every setting is client-side video, HUD or audio: the server never sees any of it, so the world, mobs, items, recipes and quests are identical by construction. 'why' gives one line per setting: what it buys, and what it costs in looks. Section keys: options_txt (vanilla options.txt, key:value), angelica_options (merged into config/angelica-options.json), angelica_modules (config/angelica-modules.cfg, Forge B:/I:/S:/D: keys), shaders (config/shaders.properties + shaderpacks/<pack>.txt), optifine (the OptiFine E7 fallback client only), mods_aside (jar-name prefixes moved out of mods/), jvm (Prism memory by installed RAM).
title: Lite: the same pack, shaded, on an ordinary PC
hardware: GTX 1060 6 GB / RX 580 class GPU, 4-6 cores, 8-16 GB RAM, 1920x1080

why.options_txt.renderDistance: 6 = the friends' server's view-distance. The server sends no chunk past 6, so this costs nothing there and the fog lands on the edge of the loaded world instead of showing a hard cut. In singleplayer you see two chunks less.
why.options_txt.fancyGraphics: Fast graphics: opaque leaves (the worst case is Twilight Forest and jungle canopies), no entity blob shadows, fast rain. The single largest vanilla lever on both CPU and GPU. Looks: solid leaf blocks.
why.options_txt.ao: Smooth lighting Minimum. Celeritas renders Minimum and Maximum alike, so no visible change here; the E7 fallback gets its cheaper mode.
why.options_txt.particles: Decreased (0 All, 1 Decreased, 2 Minimal): about half the particles in fights and rain. Looks: thinner particle storms.
why.options_txt.mipmapLevels: 2 mip levels instead of 4: the per-tick re-mip of animated textures is cheaper, distant blocks still filtered. Looks: a little more shimmer far away.
why.options_txt.anisotropicFiltering: Vanilla key, 1 = off. Angelica filters through texture_filter_mode; the E7 fallback keeps AF off.
why.options_txt.maxFps: Cap at 90. Uncapped, menus and caves run the GPU flat out, which heats a laptop into throttling and lowers the frame rate where it matters. Nothing visible on a 60 Hz monitor.
why.options_txt.enableVsync: Off; Angelica paces frames through vsync_mode.
why.options_txt.clouds: Clouds stay on: Angelica's VBO clouds are one cheap draw, and with the shader pack on the pack draws its own sky anyway.
why.options_txt.fboEnable: Framebuffer objects on; required by every shader loader.
why.options_txt.advancedOpengl: Vanilla occlusion queries off (Angelica culls on its own).
why.angelica_options.quality.biome_blend_rad: 1 block of biome blending in the cheaper FAST mode instead of 3 FANCY: less chunk-build work on a 4-core CPU. Looks: biome borders are a short gradient instead of a wide one (0 would show hard lines).
why.angelica_options.quality.grass_quality: FAST: plain grass block sides, no overlay texture. Looks: the old grass block side.
why.angelica_options.quality.use_celeritas_s: Kept on: corner shading is what keeps caves readable, and Celeritas computes it on worker threads.
why.angelica_options.quality.texture_filter_: Hardware anisotropic filtering only, no RGSS: a quarter of the texture samples per pixel, and AF is nearly free on a discrete GPU. Looks: distant floors stay sharp; slightly more shimmer than RGSS.
why.angelica_options.advanced.vsync_mode: OFF: the maxFps cap paces frames without vsync's input lag.
why.angelica_options.performance: Celeritas's culling and deferral switches on (its defaults): entity and fog occlusion culling, block-face culling, deferred chunk updates, only visible textures animated. No cost in looks.
why.angelica_options.reducer: Angelica's FPS reducer: 10 fps while another window has focus, 30 fps after 5 idle minutes, menus capped. Nothing changes while you play; it stops the game cooking the PC while you are in Discord.
why.angelica_modules.B:enableDynamicLights: Dynamic lights off: a held torch or a blaze no longer re-renders the chunks around it as it moves. That re-render is CPU work a 4-6 core PC feels. Looks: a held torch lights nothing until you place it.
why.angelica_modules.B:showSplashMemoryBar: Angelica's loading-screen memory bar off: it would draw over the Quest Forge mural.
why.shaders: The QuestForge pack at QF_PRESET 1 (Low): the physically based sky, sun shadows to 48 blocks (your own shadow but no other entities, 1024 map, hard-edged), the water model, TAA, auto-exposure, bloom, waving leaves and emissives. Drops volumetric clouds (a 2D layer instead), volumetric light, SSR (sky reflections only), GTAO (vanilla AO at 0.6), wet puddles and soft shadows. Budget: 5 ms of shader cost at 1080p on a GTX 1060 (docs/design/shaders/performance-rules.md). if_missing 'off': if the QuestForge pack is not in shaderpacks/, shaders are turned off rather than left on a heavier pack.
why.optifine: OptiFine E7 fallback client only. Shaders OFF and Fast Render ON (legal only with shaders off: it breaks every shader pack on E7), Smooth FPS off (a glFinish stall per frame), Fast Math, fast fog/clouds/trees/water/rain, dynamic lights off, smooth biomes off, no void or dripping particles.
why.mods_aside.SoundFilters: Cave reverb and muffling through walls. It ray-traces block occlusion for every sound it plays; a mob fight plays dozens at once. Content: none (the server has no such jar).
why.mods_aside.MobDismemberment: Gore: severed limbs as extra physics entities when mobs die. Content: none.
why.mods_aside.MobAmputation: The same gore for player-like mobs. Content: none.
why.mods_aside.CustomMenu: The branded title-screen buttons (11 Mpx of button art in VRAM). The mural splash and the menu music stay (QuestForgeTweaks carries them). Content: none; title screen only.
why.jvm: 3 GB on an 8 GB PC, 4 GB with 12 GB or more: the pack's live heap is 1.3 GB (measured), Angelica adds about 95 MB. On 8 GB never go higher: Windows, Discord and a browser need the rest, and swapping stutters far worse than a smaller heap.
